document.title: Your Meeting with Pakistani President Musharraf (Memorandum for the President)
document.authors: Secretary of State Colin Powell to President George W. Bush (Department of State)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Powell highlights changes in U.S.-Pakistan relations since 9/11, including cooperation on counterterrorism, nonproliferation, protection of Pakistani nuclear assets and economic development. Musharraf allied with the U.S. at considerable political risk, abandoning the Taliban and freezing terrorist assets. He is pressing for a future Afghan government supportive of Pakistan's interests and fears the Northern Alliance will occupy Kabul.

mentions.quote: President Musharraf's decision to fully cooperate with the United States in the wake of September 11, at considerable political risk, abruptly turned our stalled relationship around.
Musharraf is pressing for a future government supportive of its interests and is concerned that the Northern Alliance will occupy Kabul.

key_claims: Musharraf's post-9/11 cooperation reversed the stalled US-Pakistan relationship at considerable political risk.
Musharraf abandoned the Taliban, froze terrorist assets and quelled anti-Western protests.
Musharraf wanted a future Afghan government supportive of Pakistan's interests and feared Northern Alliance control of Kabul.
Kashmir tensions threatened US efforts in Afghanistan and risked Indo-Pakistani conflict.
US offered Pakistan economic aid including $100M budget support, $500M planned, and a $73M border security package.
